sentences.text: All sentences are directed to run concurrently Heard Mr. Jitendra Shukla, learned counsel for the appellant.
Also heard Mr. Hari Om Rai, Panel Lawyer, appearing for the respondent/State on the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the offence.

The victim, who is major girl having love affair with the appellant and she herself eloped with him on her own will without raising any objection and encroached in making consensual physical relation with the appellant.
There is no legally admissible evidence produced by the prosecution with respect to the age of the victim.
The prosecution has tried to prove the age of the victim on the basis of the Kotwari Panzi which has not been proved in accordance with law.
Even from the evidence of parents of the victim her age has not been proved that she was minor on the date of incident.
Since she herself eloped with the appellant and engaged in making consensual physical relation, no offence of kidnapping or rape is appears to be made out against the appellant.
There is no injuries found on the body of the victim and even the FSL report has not been produced by the prosecution.
The appellant was on bail during trial and has not misused the liberty granted to him.
Presently the appellant in jail since 21.01.2024 and final adjudication of the case will take it own time, therefore, he may be enlarged on bail during the pendency of the appeal.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes and have submitted that there is sufficient evidence against the appellant on record from the Kotwari register she was found to be minor and she was subjected to sexual intercourse by the appellant who is a minor girl, therefore, the appellant is not entitled for bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, considering the nature of allegation and the evidence available on record, particularly the evidence of the victim (PW-2),
medical evidence available on record and also the age of the victim and the evidence available with respect to her age and also considering that the appellant was on bail during trial and final adjudication of the case will take its own time, therefore, we are inclined to release the appellant on bail.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellant Tapan Kumar Munna by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.

He shall be released on bail on his executing personal bond of Rs.
25,000/- with one surety of the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 28.02.2025.

He shall thereafter, appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, I.A. No. 1 of 2024 filed by appellant is allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only confined for disposal of aforesaid I.A. filed in this appeal and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the Tapan Kumar Munna vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162997558/
